name: Carrholt Lakefront Parka
description: A brutally practical heavy parka designed for the Chicago-Milwaukee lakefront corridor, where winter wind off the water cuts like a blade. The Carrholt Lakefront is filled with recycled synthetic down rated to -30°C, wrapped in a matte-finished ripstop shell that sheds sleet and spray without pretension. Available in three colorways: slate gray, rust brown, and a faded olive that seems to have been designed to look worn from day one. The hood is oversized, adjustable with a single-hand cinch cord, and lined with a short pile fleece that actually keeps ears warm. Four exterior pockets, two interior, and a chest pocket with a waterproof zipper. The fit is boxy enough to layer over thick sweaters or light augmentation frames without binding. This is the coat people actually wear in Meridian 88 winters — not stylish, not augmented, just deeply, honestly warm.
what_it_says: You are a person who has stood at a bus stop in February wind coming off Lake Michigan and decided never again to be cold. Practicality over fashion, comfort over statement.
worn_by: anyone who walks to work in winter
story_hooks: A distinctive rust-brown Carrholt parka was the last thing a missing person was seen wearing — three witnesses placed her at the lakefront transit hub, but the coat turned up in a Tier 1 resale rack with the lining cut out
Carrholt's newest batch shipped with a factory defect: the chest pocket zipper pull is stamped with what appears to be a corponation logo that Carrholt denies any relationship with
The coat's oversized hood has become a low-tech counter-surveillance tool on the Shelf — no tech required, just pull it forward and most facial recognition loses confidence below 60%
